ai-at-work.title: Plaud says its software business topped $100M in ARR after shipping over 2M AI notetakers
ai-at-work.excerpt: Plaud is trying to make a mark in a crowded market full of AI-powered meeting notetakers.
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Plaud hit $100M in annual recurring revenue by shipping over 2 million AI notetakers into the market. For digital workplace teams, this signals that AI-assisted meeting documentation has moved from nice-to-have to table stakes, which means your organization needs a solid strategy around what gets recorded, who owns the data, and how it actually gets used. The crowded market is good news for buyers but bad news for IT teams who'll spend the next two years managing yet another tool that promises to save time but mostly just creates more transcripts nobody reads.

ai-at-work.title: Robinhood’s note on 10% layoffs shows blaming AI isn’t cutting it
ai-at-work.excerpt: Unlike many of his tech industry peers who have cut thousands of jobs citing the need to restructure to make the most of AI, Robinhood's CEO Vlad Tenev conspicuously made no mention of AI in his note
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Robinhood's CEO laid off 10% of staff without the usual "we're pivoting to AI" excuse that's become Silicon Valley's favorite layoff justification. This matters because it signals that workers and investors are finally getting tired of the AI smokescreen and expecting honest communication about business decisions. Tenev's silence on AI is actually refreshing, even if the outcome is the same, because at least he's not insulting our intelligence by pretending a chatbot is the real reason people are losing their jobs.

ai-at-work.title: Sweeping Android 17 update brings new AI capabilities and features to Pixel smartphones
ai-at-work.excerpt: Google LLC today dropped the latest version of its Android operating system for mobile devices, and it’s rolling out to Pixel smartphone users first of all. It’s a pretty sweeping update, introducing
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google released Android 17 with major AI features, new communication tools, and security upgrades, rolling out first to Pixel phones. Digital workplace pros need to pay attention because these updates affect how employees access corporate systems, handle sensitive data, and collaborate on mobile devices, which means IT teams better start planning compatibility testing now. Here's the thing: every time Google dumps a feature-heavy OS update on the market, someone in your organization is going to want to use it immediately, and your security team is going to have a minor heart attack.

ai-at-work.title: China’s DeepSeek reportedly raises $7.4B in funding at $50B+ valuation
ai-at-work.excerpt: Chinese artificial intelligence lab DeepSeek has reportedly raised more than 50 billion yuan, or $7.4 billion, in new funding. The Information and the Wall Street Journal today cited sources as saying
ai-at-work.dwp_take: A Chinese AI startup called DeepSeek just raised $7.4 billion and hit a $50 billion valuation, making it China's most valuable AI company. This matters because workplace tech leaders need to pay attention to who's funding AI development outside the US, since it affects everything from tool availability to competitive positioning in the enterprise space. Honestly, if you're still treating AI as a future-state problem rather than a now-state competitive threat, you're already behind.

tools-tech.title: Amazon has discounted a Lenovo IdeaPad for 73% off, and it's actually worth considering
tools-tech.excerpt: Over at Amazon, the Lenovo IdeaPad 1i has dropped to $300, making it one of the best laptop deals available on the platform.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Amazon is selling a Lenovo IdeaPad 1i laptop for $300, down 73% from its original price. For digital workplace folks managing device budgets and remote work setups, this matters because affordable hardware that doesn't completely fall apart is genuinely hard to find. That said, before you load up your cart thinking you've cracked the code on employee devices, remember that a screaming deal on a budget laptop still gets you a budget laptop, so check those specs carefully or your IT team will be hearing about it.

tools-tech.title: Android 17 is out now, with a fresh Pixel Drop for June - here's what's new
tools-tech.excerpt: You're getting productivity tricks, bubbles, new AI models, upgraded security, and more.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google dropped Android 17 with the June Pixel update, adding productivity features, new AI capabilities, improved security, and messaging bubbles to the mix. Digital workplace folks need to care because every OS update means potential compatibility headaches with enterprise apps, security policy changes, and user support tickets flooding in on day one. Here's the reality: another quarter, another "revolutionary" AI feature nobody asked for, while half your organization is still running Android 12 wondering what happened to their email app.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft says you don’t need another email security tool; experts say, not so fast
tools-tech.excerpt: Despite best efforts by defenders, malicious emails continue to slip through the cybersecurity cracks, leading some enterprises to implement a layered “defense in depth” strategy that incorporates mul
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft claims their built-in email security is sufficient and that layering additional tools provides minimal benefit, but security researchers disagree and recommend a multi-layered defense approach anyway. This matters because many organizations are caught between trusting their existing Microsoft investment and the real-world evidence that determined attackers still get through single-layer defenses. Here's the thing: Microsoft has every incentive to say their tool is enough, and I've seen enough breaches to know that relying on any single vendor's promise, no matter how good their product actually is, tends to end badly.

tools-tech.title: Anthropic’s new privacy policy offers US consumers a way around the Fable ban
tools-tech.excerpt: Anthropic’s apparent inability to identify which of its users are foreign nationals has led to some collateral damage from a US export ban on its most powerful AI models — but there is a way around it
tools-tech.dwp_take: Anthropic got slapped with a US export ban on its newest AI models and can't actually tell who's foreign versus domestic, so they're letting Americans opt into a privacy policy that basically says "trust us, we won't share your data with foreigners." This matters because if your organization is counting on cutting-edge AI tools for knowledge work, you're potentially looking at access restrictions, compliance headaches, and the awkward reality that AI companies haven't figured out basic identity verification. The real kicker is that Anthropic's solution amounts to asking users to pinky-swear they're American, which feels like the digital equivalent of an honor system at a bank.

digital-culture.title: Why employers should treat domestic violence as a workplace issue
digital-culture.excerpt: In a small West Virginia county a few years ago, Wanda (pseudonym) asked her employer for some time off to deal with a situation at home. Her employer turned her down. Not long after, Wanda’s situatio
digital-culture.dwp_take: Employers are increasingly recognizing that domestic violence isn't just a personal problem, it's a workplace safety and productivity issue that demands policy responses and support structures. For digital workplace professionals, this means building inclusive benefits platforms, flexible work policies, and resource access into your systems because your workforce's safety directly affects your organizational health. The hard truth is that treating domestic violence as someone else's problem is not only morally indefensible, it's bad business that costs companies money and occasionally, as in Wanda's case, puts everyone at risk.

digital-culture.title: Robinhood lays off 10% of staff to flatten its organizational structure
digital-culture.excerpt: In a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) filing on Tuesday, Robinhood said it would cut 10% of its full-time workforce of 2,900 and close a “small number” of open roles. The Menlo Park, Californi
digital-culture.dwp_take: Robinhood is cutting 10% of its workforce while eliminating middle management layers to reduce costs and bureaucracy. This matters because it's the latest example of companies betting that flatter hierarchies improve decision-making and agility, which puts pressure on digital workplace tools to handle broader spans of control. The irony is that executives always claim they're cutting bloat, but somehow the tools budget survives intact every time.

digital-culture.title: The power of personal branding
digital-culture.excerpt: When I published The Most Powerful Woman in the Room Is You in 2019, I thought I was launching a book. I didn’t realize it at the time, but what I was actually building was a brand. In my first meetin
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company piece explores how the author accidentally built a personal brand while launching a book in 2019, starting with a snap decision on red and pink color palettes. For digital workplace folks, this matters because personal branding directly impacts how you're perceived internally, your career trajectory, and whether people actually remember who you are beyond your job title. Here's the thing though: most people overthink personal branding like it's rocket science when really it's just being consistently yourself across platforms and actually showing up.

digital-culture.title: ‘Pretty Crazy’ Token Usage Is Testing Bosses’ Bet on AI
digital-culture.excerpt: A Silicon Valley software maker and an ecommerce company reveal to WIRED how they are navigating the emerging challenge of “tokenomics.”
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are discovering that AI models consume way more tokens (basically the building blocks of AI processing) than expected, creating serious budget headaches and forcing IT leaders to rethink their AI strategies. This matters because digital workplace leaders are getting pressure to deploy AI everywhere, but the actual costs of running these systems at scale are turning out to be a lot messier than the vendor pitch decks suggested. After three decades in this space, I can tell you this is just the latest reminder that technology adoption always looks cheaper on a spreadsheet than it does in reality, and someone's going to have some awkward conversations with finance.

industry-news.title: Infinite Campus: Salesforce Breach Exposed 137,000 Staff Records
industry-news.excerpt: Infinite Campus says a Salesforce breach exposed data tied to 137,000 school staff accounts, raising phishing and SaaS security concerns. The post Infinite Campus: Salesforce Breach Exposed 137,000 St
industry-news.dwp_take: A Salesforce vulnerability exposed personal data for 137,000 school employees through Infinite Campus, a widely used student information system. This matters because schools are increasingly relying on cloud platforms to manage sensitive employee and student data, and breaches like this one expose the real security gaps between vendors and the institutions trusting them. Here's the thing: if your organization thinks "we use Salesforce so we're secure" you're already behind, because security is a chain and Infinite Campus just proved the links are weaker than advertised.

industry-news.title: Nvidia Eyes $20B Debt Sale as AI Cash Flow Soars
industry-news.excerpt: Nvidia’s planned debt sale could top $20 billion, giving enterprise buyers another look at its cash flow, debt profile, and AI financing plans. The post Nvidia Eyes $20B Debt Sale as AI Cash Flow Soar
industry-news.dwp_take: Nvidia is planning a massive $20 billion debt sale, capitalizing on strong AI-driven cash flows to raise capital for growth and shareholder returns. This matters to digital workplace professionals because it signals where the big money is flowing, which determines what technologies get funded, what gets shelved, and ultimately what tools your organization will be pressured to adopt in the next few years. If you're not already getting questions about generative AI implementation in your workplace strategy, buckle up because this kind of cash burn by Nvidia tells you those questions are coming whether you're ready or not.

industry-news.title: SpaceX to Acquire Cursor in $60B Stock Deal, Deepening Elon Musk’s AI Empire
industry-news.excerpt: SpaceX will buy Cursor parent Anysphere in a $60B all-stock deal, giving Elon Musk’s company a major AI coding asset days after its IPO. The post SpaceX to Acquire Cursor in $60B Stock Deal, Deepening
industry-news.dwp_take: SpaceX just dropped $60 billion in stock to buy Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, an AI coding tool that's been gaining real traction with developers. For digital workplace folks, this matters because AI-assisted coding is moving from nice-to-have to table-stakes, and when a rocket company with unlimited resources decides this is worth massive capital, your enterprise tooling strategy needs updating. Elon's basically saying "I'm betting the farm on AI developers" right after an IPO, which is either visionary or a sign he's betting on every shiny thing that moves these days, honestly.

industry-news.title: Apple Watch Blood Sugar Tracking: Latest Timeline, Patents, and Challenges
industry-news.excerpt: Apple Watch blood sugar tracking remains unconfirmed. Here's the latest on the timeline, patents, technical challenges, and what Apple Watch can do now. The post Apple Watch Blood Sugar Tracking: Late
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple is still working on blood sugar tracking for the Apple Watch, but it's not ready yet and faces real technical hurdles that keep pushing the timeline back. For digital workplace leaders, this matters because wearable health data will eventually become part of how we track employee wellness programs, and you need to understand what's actually possible versus what's vaporware.
